proposed_from.topic: Complete binary three-item target-law classification under MNAR conditional missingness DAGs. For every labelled DAG G on binary X=(X1,X2,X3) and R=(R1,R2,R3), allow arbitrary Xj-to-Ri arrows, an acyclic R subgraph, no R-to-X arrows or latent variables, and every strictly positive 64-cell law factorizing as p(X) times the response kernels. Construct a total deterministic Complete3 classifier for uniform graph-model identification of the eight-cell target p_X from the full coarsened observed law. Its ID output must give eight rational expressions in observed cell probabilities, with divisions only by observed marginals positive throughout the model and a graph-factorization derivation. Its NONID output must give two explicit strictly positive rational 64-cell Markov laws with identical probabilities for all 27 coarsened observed cells but different p_X at a named cell. Prove that Complete3 terminates under an explicit graph-uniform operation bound B and returns ID iff p_X is uniformly identified, otherwise NONID, for all 12,800 labelled graphs. The construction may combine intervention-tree fixing, conditional independence, Chen odds-ratio factorization, grouped partial-order fixing, exact enumeration, and a finite obstruction catalogue, but may not use generic real quantifier elimination as the completeness proof. On every fixed epsilon-interior subclass, derive the plug-in rational estimator's multinomial influence function, covariance estimator, and simultaneous confidence region for all target cells. The public flexMissing intervention-tree workflow is the consumer: accepted graphs gain estimable formulas and rejected graphs gain checkable positive certificates. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Exact rational calculations verify the odds-rescue model (27 observed cells, minimum full mass 1/180, odds ratios 2 and 9/4, all eight target cells recovered as 1/8), the supplied self-censoring twins, and a new positive criss-cross twin fiber. Exhaustive graph reductions give positive rational twins for 11,854 labelled graphs and known/direct formulas for 742, leaving 204 graphs in 34 relabeling classes; an independently coded but unaudited fixing-state search leaves 48 graphs in eight classes. Checks distinguished uniform from law-specific identification, interior from boundary witnesses, and graph-specific certificates from generic algebraic decidability. The resolved March 2026 talk abstract reports partial solutions and remaining failures, and no public K=3 theorem was found through 2026-09-05. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove for every residual representative either a uniform rational observed-marginal functional or strictly positive rational observational twins, then compile certificates into a sound terminating classifier with an explicit operation bound. EARLY KILL TEST: Audit the fixing-state search and solve residual case 6, including positive rank-degenerate strata; stop if it forces a non-rational inverse, a forbidden divisor, or only irrational nonidentifying fibers. seed_details.one_line: Construct a total \(\operatorname{Complete}_3\) classifier returning denominator-safe rational formulas or explicit positive rational twins, with an iff theorem and operation bound.

anchor.proof_boundary: The full-law obstruction proof is complete, but the Conclusion states that target-law completeness remains open because target recovery can survive full-law failure.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Replace the full-law obstruction dichotomy by a target-fibre certificate dichotomy that permits fixing and odds-ratio rescue before constructing graph-factorized twins.
seed_details.destination_search: Exact searches for three-item target-law completeness and intervention-tree plus odds-ratio completeness found the 2020 full-law theorem, the 2026 sound-only tree paper, and no public \(K=3\) classification theorem through September 5, 2026.
adjacent_threads: pmlr-v115-bhattacharya20b supplies grouped partial-order fixing but leaves completeness and efficient search open.
GuoNabi2026InterventionTree supplies the executable tree, its soundness theorem, and an explicit odds-ratio false negative.
TikkaKarvanen2024 supplies categorical colluder equations under rank restrictions, not graph-uniform target recovery.
DuarteEtAl2023 supplies a polynomial-program audit oracle without rational certificate extraction.
seed_details.key_part_adapted: The setup and motivation follow GuoNabi2026InterventionTree Sections 1--2; the hybrid proof adapts pmlr-v115-bhattacharya20b Proposition 1 and pmlr-v119-nabi20a Scenario 1 and Theorem 2.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is immediate from the 2020 completeness theorem because target laws are marginals of full laws.
seed_details.rebuttal: Full-law identification is sufficient but not necessary for target-law identification, as the anchor states and colluder examples demonstrate; the necessity proof and certificate language must therefore change.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not a finite lookup claim: it requires a uniform iff theorem, graph-factorization proofs, positive rational witnesses, an explicit operation bound, and a separate open residual dichotomy.

seed_details.one_line: Build a finite minimal-obstruction catalogue whose every target-law obstruction carries a reusable strictly positive rational twin family and whose graph reductions cover every nonidentified input.

anchor.proof_boundary: Self-censoring and colluders are complete obstructions for the full law, but colluders can leave the target law identified.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Construct paired graph-Markov conditional tables that preserve all \(27\) coarsened cells while changing one target coordinate, rather than perturbing an ambient response simplex.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches located the criss-cross construction in GuoZhaoNabi2023 and polynomial feasibility in DuarteEtAl2023, but no positive rational basis and lifting theorem for all binary three-item failures.
adjacent_threads: pmlr-v115-bhattacharya20b Lemma 1 gives colluder full-law twins but also shows target-law survival is possible.
GuoZhaoNabi2023 supplies the nearest criss-cross observational-equivalence analysis.
DuarteEtAl2023 supplies exact finite polynomial feasibility for discovering candidate twin fibres.
TikkaKarvanen2024 explains why standard binary countermodel constructions may be inadequate in categorical missingness problems.
seed_details.key_part_adapted: The obstruction-to-paired-laws architecture follows pmlr-v119-nabi20a Theorem 2, but the first altered step targets a marginal coordinate and enforces strict rational positivity after coarsening.
seed_details.referee_objection: The full-law self-censoring and colluder witnesses already form the required obstruction catalogue.
seed_details.rebuttal: A colluder need not destroy the target law, so full-law twins do not classify target fibres; each retained obstruction must alter \(p_X\) after coarsening and respect the graph factorization.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The witness is required as a rational family or lifted template over a nondegenerate positive region, not one hand-tuned table.

seed_details.one_line: Separate graph-uniform target-law identification from rank-generic recovery by resolving every strictly positive rank-degenerate stratum in three-item colluder graphs.

anchor.proof_boundary: Categorical colluder equations identify the full law under full-rank conditions, while rank failure does not decide unrestricted target-law recovery.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: At determinant zero, replace matrix inversion by a stratum-specific target-fibre analysis and either find another positive-marginal formula or construct an exact positive twin direction.
seed_details.destination_search: The destination search found LiMiaoShpitserTchetgenTchetgen2023 and GuoZhaoNabi2023 under completeness or parametric restrictions, but no unrestricted graph-uniform exceptional-stratum theorem.

seed_details.key_part_adapted: The colluder-matrix construction of TikkaKarvanen2024 Theorems 1--2 is retained on full-rank strata; the new step begins exactly where the Moore--Penrose inverse ceases to be a uniform observed-marginal formula.
seed_details.referee_objection: Rank failure already implies nonidentification by elementary linear algebra.
seed_details.rebuttal: Failure to identify a response kernel does not imply failure to identify its target marginal, and a rank-deficient system can retain a unique target functional.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim is uniform over complete positive strata and explicitly excludes a generic-rank shortcut.

seed_details.one_line: Prove that every uniformly identified binary three-item target cell lies in the observed rational function field localized at positive marginals, or exhibit a graph with an unavoidable algebraic inverse.

anchor.proof_boundary: Polynomial programs decide sharp fibres but do not imply that a singleton fibre is a rational function of observed probabilities.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Exploit the triangular binary conditional-response factorization before elimination to test rational field membership rather than only singleton feasibility.
seed_details.destination_search: No paper found in the targeted search proves rational generation for the three-item coarsening map; generic algebraic-identifiability sources expressly distinguish rational from algebraic inversion.
seed_details.referee_objection: Finite discrete identification always yields a rational formula after elimination.
seed_details.rebuttal: Polynomial singleton fibres can define non-rational algebraic roots, so a missingness-specific rational-generation argument is essential.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The object is a function-field theorem or counterexample, not generic quantifier elimination.
seed_details.decision: drop after ranking because it is a necessary subquestion of the selected classifier rather than a separate first paper

seed_details.one_line: Give a canonical pattern-provenance normal form and numerical operation bound for hybrid intervention, grouped-fixing, conditional-independence, and odds-ratio traces.

anchor.proof_boundary: Fixing kernels are sequence-invariant after reachability is established, but context-restricted missingness operations can change selection provenance.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Strengthen the fixing state by the missingness pattern and selection provenance before attempting adjacent-operation identities.
seed_details.destination_search: The grouped-fixing and intervention-tree papers supply distinct state spaces; neither gives a complete quotient normal form or worst-case bound for their hybrid.
seed_details.referee_objection: Termination is trivial because there are only \(12800\) graphs.
seed_details.rebuttal: A finite input domain does not bound an unspecified symbolic search or certify its transformations; the result requires a decreasing measure and counted trace grammar.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The algorithmic theorem is tied to semantic certificate invariants, not merely state enumeration.
seed_details.decision: drop as a supporting theorem in the selected seed

anchor.proof_boundary: The paper exhibits target-law survival despite colluders but does not characterize all graphs where the two identification notions diverge.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Intersect a complete target-law classifier with the published full-law obstruction criterion and retain explicit certificates for both sides of the divergence.
seed_details.destination_search: The full-law theorem and target-law sufficient procedures contain examples but no exhaustive binary three-item divergence catalogue.
seed_details.referee_objection: This becomes a corollary once Complete3 exists.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection holds, so this is not retained as an independent kernel.

seed_details.one_line: For every graph classified nonidentified, derive sharp graph-compatible bounds for each target cell and compile their multinomial inference.

anchor.proof_boundary: Polynomial programs deliver sharp bounds for a supplied finite model but not closed-form graph-wide three-item bound certificates.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Condition the response-function program on the exact conditional-MNAR factorization and seek reusable analytic endpoint certificates by obstruction class.
seed_details.destination_search: The targeted search found general automated bounds and classical missing-data bounds, but no all-graph binary three-item sharp-bound catalogue.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is simply running an existing polynomial bounder \(12800\) times.
seed_details.rebuttal: Without closed-form or reusable graph certificates the objection holds; the present evidence does not yet support the stronger analytic claim.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The proposed bounds would need graph-native endpoint witnesses and an inference rung, not a black-box program.

seed_details.one_line: Characterize the minimal certificate basis whose closure reproduces the union of intervention-tree, grouped-fixing, and odds-ratio target-law acceptances.

anchor.proof_boundary: The paper asks whether different parameterizations can be systematically combined into a sound-and-complete procedure.

seed_details.first_changed_proof_step: Define a common kernel-state semantics before comparing syntactic acceptance sets and proving irredundancy of operations.
seed_details.destination_search: No common finite semantic basis was located; grouped fixing and intervention trees use distinct state objects, and odds ratios are not fixing steps.
seed_details.referee_objection: A union of three sound procedures is mechanically sound and needs no theorem.
seed_details.rebuttal: Sound union is immediate, but minimality and completeness are not; absent the latter, this seed is too procedural to lead.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The seed is not selected because it risks becoming a software-normalization paper without the residual iff result.

proposed_from.literature_map: Nabi, Bhattacharya, and Shpitser (ICML 2020, Theorems 1--2, Scenario 1, Conclusion) prove full-law completeness by a Chen odds-ratio construction and explicit obstruction argument, while stating that target-law completeness remains open. Bhattacharya, Nabi, Shpitser, and Robins (UAI 2020, Proposition 1, Proposition 2, Lemma 2, Section 6) provide grouped partial-order fixing and selection subproblems as sufficient target-law machinery without a complete efficient search. Guo and Nabi (2026, Algorithm 1, Theorem 1, Corollary 2, Figure E.2(a), Section 8) provide the closest executable workflow; the paper explicitly identifies its odds-ratio false negative and asks for a sound-and-complete hybrid. Tikka and Karvanen (2024, Theorems 1--2, Section 8) turn categorical colluders into identifiable matrix equations under rank conditions, creating the exact generic-versus-uniform boundary that Complete3 must resolve. Li, Miao, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (Biometrics 2023) recover a self-censoring model under completeness, not over the unrestricted graph class. Guo, Zhao, and Nabi (UAI 2023, Theorem 1, Sections 4--5) treat criss-cross MNAR with parametric or rank restrictions and semiparametric odds-ratio estimation. Richardson, Evans, Robins, and Shpitser (Annals of Statistics 2023, Proposition 25 and Theorem 31) supply fixing-kernel invariance after reachability, but not under missingness-pattern context restriction. Duarte et al. (JASA 2023, Theorem 1 and Sections 4--6) provide a polynomial feasibility and bounds oracle suitable for discovery checks, not the rational graphical certificate theorem. Malinsky, Shpitser, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (JASA 2022), Chen (Annals of Statistics 2022), and Bhattacharya, Nabi, and Shpitser (JMLR 2022) supply adjacent influence-function constructions. Targeted searches through September 5, 2026 found no public theorem classifying all \(12800\) labelled binary three-item graphs; the closest 2026 intervention-tree paper still labels completeness open.
